    98	/-! ### Definition -/
    99	
   100	/-- The wave Green measure `G_s` on `ℝ^d` (main TeX lines 709, 5109-5113;
   101	Chen (2.5)): `d = 1`: `½ 1_{|x|<s} dx`; `d = 2`:
   102	`1_{|x|<s} dx / (2π√(s²-|x|²))`; `d = 3`: `σ_s/(4πs)`, written as
   103	`(s/(4π)) · map (ω ↦ sω) volume.toSphere`, which takes Mathlib's
   104	`Measure.toSphere` as the surface measure of the unit sphere (a definitional
   105	choice, Le's decision 4; see the module doc); other `d`: `0`. -/
   106	def waveGreen : (d : ℕ) → ℝ → Measure (Rd d)
   107	  | 1, s => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2) • volume.restrict (ball 0 s)
   108	  | 2, s => volume.withDensity ((ball (0 : Rd 2) s).indicator
   109	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹))
   110	  | 3, s => ENNReal.ofReal (s / (4 * π)) •
   111	      (volume.toSphere.map fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => s • (ω : Rd 3))
   112	  | _, _ => 0
   113	
   114	/-- Outside `d ∈ {1,2,3}` the definition is the zero measure (a convention;
   115	the manuscript has `d ∈ {1,2,3}`). -/
   116	theorem waveGreen_other (d : ℕ) (h1 : d ≠ 1) (h2 : d ≠ 2) (h3 : d ≠ 3) (s : ℝ) :
   117	    waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   118	  unfold waveGreen; split <;> simp_all
   119	
   120	/-- For `s ≤ 0` the wave Green measure is zero (in `d = 1, 2` the ball is
   121	empty, in `d = 3` the factor `s/(4π)` is `≤ 0`). -/
   122	theorem waveGreen_of_nonpos (d : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : s ≤ 0) : waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   123	  by_cases h1 : d = 1
   124	  · subst h1; simp [waveGreen, ball_eq_empty.2 hs]
   125	  by_cases h2 : d = 2
   126	  · subst h2; simp [waveGreen, ball_eq_empty.2 hs]
   127	  by_cases h3 : d = 3
   128	  · subst h3
   129	    have : s / (4 * π) ≤ 0 := div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg hs (by positivity)
   130	    simp [waveGreen, ENNReal.ofReal_eq_zero.2 this]
   131	  exact waveGreen_other d h1 h2 h3 s

   135	/-- `Γ(3/2) = √π/2`.  Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/

   137	  rw [Real.Gamma_add_one (by norm_num), Real.Gamma_one_half_eq]; ring
   138	
   139	/-- Mass in `d = 1`: `G_s(ℝ) = s` for `s > 0`. -/
   140	theorem mass_one (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) : waveGreen 1 s univ = ENNReal.ofReal s := by
   141	  simp only [waveGreen, Measure.smul_apply, Measure.restrict_apply MeasurableSet.univ,
   142	    univ_inter, EuclideanSpace.volume_ball, smul_eq_mul]
   143	  simp only [Fintype.card_fin, pow_one, Nat.cast_one]
   144	  rw [gamma_three_halves, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity),
   145	    ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)]
   146	  congr 1
   147	  have : (0 : ℝ) < √π := Real.sqrt_pos.2 Real.pi_pos
   148	  field_simp

   150	/-- The radial density in `d = 2`, `h(r) = (2π√(s²-r²))⁻¹` (it is `(2π·0)⁻¹ = 0`
   151	for `r ≥ s` by the conventions of `Real.sqrt` and `⁻¹`; only its values on
   152	`r < s` enter `waveGreen 2`).  Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   153	def radial2 (s r : ℝ) : ℝ := (2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - r ^ 2))⁻¹
   154	
   155	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   156	theorem radial2_nonneg (s r : ℝ) : 0 ≤ radial2 s r := by unfold radial2; positivity
   157	
   158	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   159	theorem radial2_eq_zero (s r : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hr : s ≤ r) : radial2 s r = 0 := by
   160	  unfold radial2
   161	  rw [Real.sqrt_eq_zero'.2 (by nlinarith)]; simp
   162	
   163	/-- `r ↦ -√(s²-r²)/(2π)` is an antiderivative of `r · h(r)` on `(0,s)`.
   164	Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   165	theorem hasDerivAt_radial2 (s y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Ioo 0 s) :
   166	    HasDerivAt (fun r => -Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - r ^ 2) / (2 * π)) (y * radial2 s y) y := by
   167	  have hpos : 0 < s ^ 2 - y ^ 2 := by nlinarith [hy.1, hy.2]
   168	  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun r => s ^ 2 - r ^ 2) (-(2 * y)) y := by
   169	    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_pow 2 y).const_sub (s ^ 2))

   171	  convert h2' using 1
   172	  unfold radial2
   173	  have := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hpos
   174	  field_simp

   176	/-- `∫_0^s r h(r) dr = s/(2π)`, with integrability.  Auxiliary to the Lean
   177	proof route. -/
   178	theorem integral_radial2 (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) :
   179	    IntegrableOn (fun y => y * radial2 s y) (Ioc 0 s) ∧
   180	      ∫ y in Ioc 0 s, y * radial2 s y = s / (2 * π) := by

181	  have hc : ContinuousOn (fun r => -Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - r ^ 2) / (2 * π)) (Icc 0 s) := by
   182	    fun_prop
   183	  have hI := intervalIntegral.integrableOn_deriv_of_nonneg hc
   184	    (fun y hy => hasDerivAt_radial2 s y hy) (fun y hy => mul_nonneg hy.1.le (radial2_nonneg s y))
   185	  refine ⟨hI, ?_⟩
   186	  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hs.le,
   187	    intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right_of_le hs.le hc
   188	      (fun y hy => (hasDerivAt_radial2 s y hy).hasDerivWithinAt)
   189	      ((intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le hs.le).2 hI)]
   190	  simp [Real.sqrt_sq hs.le]
   191	  field_simp

   193	/-- Mass in `d = 2`: `G_s(ℝ²) = s` for `s > 0`. -/
   194	theorem mass_two (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) : waveGreen 2 s univ = ENNReal.ofReal s := by

   196	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹)) =
   197	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (radial2 s ‖x‖) := by
   198	    funext x
   199	    by_cases hx : x ∈ ball (0 : Rd 2) s
   200	    · simp [hx, radial2]
   201	    · rw [indicator_of_notMem hx, radial2_eq_zero s _ hs.le (by simpa using hx)]; simp
   202	  have hint : IntegrableOn (fun y : ℝ => y ^ (Module.finrank ℝ (Rd 2) - 1) • radial2 s y)
   203	      (Ioi 0) := by
   204	    simp only [finrank_euclideanSpace, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul]
   205	    have := (integral_radial2 s hs).1
   206	    rw [show Ioi (0 : ℝ) = Ioc 0 s ∪ Ioi s from (Ioc_union_Ioi_eq_Ioi hs.le).symm]
   207	    refine this.congr_fun (fun y _ => by simp) measurableSet_Ioc |>.union ?_
   208	    refine integrableOn_zero.congr_fun (fun y hy => ?_) measurableSet_Ioi
   209	    simp [radial2_eq_zero s y hs.le (le_of_lt hy)]

   120	/-! ### Definitions -/
   121	
   122	/-- The supplied input for `N₀`: the mass identity `G_s(ℝ^d) = s` for `s > 0`
   123	(proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, line 825), stated for a family `G` of
   124	measures on `ℝ^d` standing for the wave Green measures, which this package
   125	does not define. -/
   126	structure GreenMass (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) : Prop where
   127	  mass : ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → G s univ = ENNReal.ofReal s
   128	
   129	/-- `N₀(θ) = ∫_0^∞ e^{-θs} G_s(ℝ^d) ds` (`E:damped-norm-definitions`, line 747),
   130	for a family `G` of measures on `ℝ^d`. -/
   131	def N0 (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   132	  ∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Real.exp (-(θ * s)) * (G s univ).toReal
   133	
   134	/-- The first norm with the Laplace variable restricted to `S`:
   135	`Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} λ^{a-1} R_Γ(θ+λ) dλ`. -/
   136	def N1on (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ :=
   137	  (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in S, l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l) ∂L0
   138	
   139	/-- `N₁^{(M)}(1)`, the first norm at `θ = 1` with `λ > M` (lines 782-784). -/
   140	def N1tail (a M : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ := N1on a 1 (Ioi M) μ
   141	
   142	/-- The temporal kernel with the Laplace variable restricted to `S`:
   143	`K_S(r) = Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} e^{-λ|r|} λ^{a-1} dλ`.  At `r = 0` with
   144	`S ∩ (0,∞)` of infinite `λ^{a-1} dλ`-mass the integral diverges and the Lean
   145	value is the junk value `0`; this happens only on the diagonal `s = t`, a
   146	`P2`-null set. -/
   147	def KS (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   148	  (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in S, subKernel a |r| l ∂L0
   149	
   150	/-- `K_M(r) = Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_M^∞ e^{-λ|r|} λ^{a-1} dλ` (lines 778-781), the
   151	`λ`-integral taken over `(M,∞) ∩ (0,∞)`. -/
   152	def KM (a M r : ℝ) : ℝ := KS a (Ioi M) r

   155	def N2onOuter (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ :=

   191	  rcases h.alpha_range with h1 | h1

   195	/-- `0 ≤ K_S(r)` (line 832 for `S = (M,∞)`). -/
   196	theorem KS_nonneg (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) : 0 ≤ KS a S r := by
   197	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   198	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   199	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl

   204	theorem KS_le (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r ≠ 0) :

   207	  have hI := subKernel_integrable a |r| ha hr'
   208	  refine ⟨hI.integrableOn, ?_⟩
   209	  rw [rpow_neg_eq_subordination a |r| ha hr', KS]
   210	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   211	  refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (setIntegral_le_integral hI ?_) (by positivity)

   242	theorem weight_scaling {μ : Measure (Rd d)} {alpha : ℝ} (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   243	    (a θ u : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hu : 0 < u) :
   244	    weight a θ μ (θ * u) = θ ^ (a + alpha - 5) * weight a 1 μ u := by
   245	  unfold weight
   246	  rw [show θ + θ * u = θ * (1 + u) by ring]
   247	  rw [resolvent_homog hI θ hθ, resolvent_homog hI (θ * (1 + u)) (by positivity),

   251	  have e : θ ^ (a + alpha - 5) = θ ^ (a - 2) * θ ^ (alpha - 2) * θ⁻¹ := by
   252	    rw [← Real.rpow_add hθ, ← Real.rpow_neg_one, ← Real.rpow_add hθ]; ring_nf
   253	  rw [e]
   254	  field_simp

   258	theorem N2sq_scaling {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   259	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   260	    N2sq alpha0 θ μ = θ ^ (-(4 - alpha - alpha0)) * N2sq alpha0 1 μ := by
   261	  have hI := spectralHomogeneous_of_homog h
   262	  have := h.μ_radon
   263	  have hR := integrable_inv_one_add_sq hI (by linarith [h.threshold, h.alpha0_pos])
   264	  have h0 := measure_zero hI (alpha_pos h)
   265	  rw [K_eq_integral_weight μ hR h0 alpha0 θ h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one hθ,
   266	    K_eq_integral_weight μ hR h0 alpha0 1 h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one one_pos]
   267	  have hc := integral_comp_mul_left_Ioi (weight alpha0 θ μ) 0 hθ
   268	  rw [mul_zero, smul_eq_mul] at hc
   269	  rw [setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi
   270	    (fun u hu => weight_scaling hI alpha0 θ u hθ hu), integral_const_mul] at hc
   271	  have e : θ ^ (-(4 - alpha - alpha0)) = θ * θ ^ (alpha0 + alpha - 5) := by
   272	    rw [show -(4 - alpha - alpha0) = 1 + (alpha0 + alpha - 5) by ring,
   273	      Real.rpow_add hθ, Real.rpow_one]
   274	  rw [e, mul_assoc, hc]
   275	  field_simp

   278	`μ(cA) = c^α μ(A)` (any `a`; lines 772-775 and 825-826 with `a = α₀`). -/
   279	theorem N1_scaling {alpha : ℝ} {μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   280	    (a θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   281	    N1 a θ μ = θ ^ (alpha + a - 2) * N1 a 1 μ := by
   282	  unfold N1
   283	  have hc := integral_comp_mul_left_Ioi (fun l => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) 0 hθ
   284	  rw [mul_zero, smul_eq_mul] at hc
   285	  have hpt : ∀ u ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), (θ * u) ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + θ * u) =
   286	      θ ^ (alpha + a - 3) * (u ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (1 + u)) := by
   287	    intro u hu
   288	    have hu0 : (0 : ℝ) < u := hu
   289	    rw [show θ + θ * u = θ * (1 + u) by ring, resolvent_homog hI _ (by positivity),
   290	      resolvent_homog hI (1 + u) (by positivity),
   291	      Real.mul_rpow hθ.le (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 + u by positivity), Real.mul_rpow hθ.le hu0.le]
   292	    have e : θ ^ (alpha + a - 3) = θ ^ (a - 1) * θ ^ (alpha - 2) := by
   293	      rw [← Real.rpow_add hθ]; ring_nf
   294	    rw [e]; ring
   295	  rw [setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi hpt, integral_const_mul] at hc
   296	  have e : θ ^ (alpha + a - 2) = θ * θ ^ (alpha + a - 3) := by
   297	    rw [show alpha + a - 2 = 1 + (alpha + a - 3) by ring, Real.rpow_add hθ, Real.rpow_one]
   298	  rw [e]

   697	\begin{lemma}[White-space test]\label{L:white-test}
   698	  For $d = \alpha = 1$ and $\gamma = \delta_0$, put $c_0 =
   699	  ((1-\alpha_0)(2-\alpha_0)(3-\alpha_0))^{-1}$. Then
   700	  \begin{equation}\label{E:white-test}
   701	    \E X_1(t,x)^2=c_0t^{3-\alpha_0},\qquad
   702	    \E X_2(t,x)=\tfrac12c_0t^{3-\alpha_0}.
   703	  \end{equation}
   704	  In particular, the total-order-two contribution to~\eqref{E:full-second} is
   705	  $2c_0t^{3-\alpha_0}$.
   706	\end{lemma}
   707	
   708	\begin{proof}
   709	  Here $G(s,y) = \frac12\mathbf1_{\{|y|<s\}}$. Therefore, $\int_\R
   710	  G(s,y)G(r,y)\ud y = \min(s,r)/2$. The $(1,1)$ integral is
   711	  \[
   712	    \int_0^t\ud s\int_0^s r(s-r)^{-\alpha_0}\ud r
   713	    =\frac{t^{3-\alpha_0}}
   714	    {(1-\alpha_0)(2-\alpha_0)(3-\alpha_0)}.
   715	  \]
   716	  For the $(0,2)$ integral, the delta covariance sets the two spatial vertices
   717	  equal. Write $0 < r < s < t$ for their ordered time variables. The first
   718	  factor $G_r$ has spatial mass $r$, while $G_{s-r}(0) = 1/2$. Its time integral
   719	  is half the preceding display. The $(2,0)$ term is identical. This proves
   720	  Lemma~\ref{L:white-test}.
   721	\end{proof}

   766	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   767	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
   768	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   769	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   770	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   771	  \[
   772	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   773	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   774	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   775	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   776	  \]
   777	  Let
   778	  \[
   779	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   780	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   781	  \]
   782	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   783	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   784	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   785	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   786	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   787	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   788	  \end{equation}
   789	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing, Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel, and
   790	  restriction of a temporal Laplace domain do not increase these corresponding
   791	  full or tail norm bounds.
   792	\end{lemma}

   794	\begin{proof}

   796	  gives $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. Radon finiteness and $\alpha > 0$ then imply
   797	  $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. In particular, $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha V$, where $V = \mu(B_1)
   798	  < \infty$. Therefore, for $a > 0$,
   799	  \[
   800	    \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{a^2+|\xi|^2}
   801	    =\alpha V a^{\alpha-2}
   802	    \int_0^\infty\frac{u^{\alpha-1}}{1+u^2}\ud u<\infty.
   803	  \]

   805	  reduces its finiteness to
   806	  $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}(\theta+\lambda)^{\alpha-2} \ud\lambda <
   807	  \infty$: the conditions at zero and infinity are $\alpha_0 > 0$ and
   808	  $\alpha+\alpha_0 < 2$.

   810	  For $N_2$ use $|\widehat{G}_s(\xi)| \le \min(s,|\xi|^{-1})$. On $|\xi| \le 1$,

   813	    V\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty

   818	  finite by splitting into $s \le t$ and $t \le s$, then using $u = \min(s,t)$

  4389	
  4390	Defines the wave Green measures `G_s` of the main file
  4391	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `975feb3`) and states
  4392	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lemma, lines 766-792; proof, lines 793-846)
  4393	with nothing supplied. Sources of the measures at `975feb3`: `d = 1`,
  4394	`G(s,y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s}` (proof of `L:white-test`, line 709; again at
  4395	lines 4055 and 7569); `d = 2, 3`, the proof of `L:higher-riesz` (lines
  4396	5106-5114), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7:
  4397	`G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2))` and
  4398	`G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h)`, `sigma_h` the surface measure of the
  4399	radius-`h` sphere, and states "Both have mass `h` and satisfy
  4400	`G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)`" (lines 5113-5114). The list of notation
  4401	(`notes/index/list-of-notation.tex`, line 102) describes `G_t` as the "Wave
  4402	Green measure, with mass `t` and support in the closed radius-`t` ball". The
  4403	mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` is the step of the proof of
  4404	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` at line 825, which `DampedNormsHomog` took as
  4405	the supplied input `GreenMass G`.
  4406	
  4407	Definition. `waveGreen d s` is, for `d = 1`, `(1/2)` Lebesgue measure
  4408	restricted to the open ball `|x| < s`; for `d = 2`, Lebesgue measure with
  4409	density `1_{|x|<s} (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - |x|^2))^(-1)` (inside the ball the root
  4410	is of a positive number, so no `sqrt` or division junk value enters); for
  4411	`d = 3`, `(s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) volume.toSphere`; for every other `d`,
  4412	the zero measure. For `d = 3` this is a DEFINITIONAL CHOICE (Le's decision 4
  4413	for wave L6): Mathlib's `Measure.toSphere` (which satisfies
  4414	`sigma(A) = 3 vol{r w : 0 < r < 1, w in A}` for measurable `A`, the cone
  4415	measure) is taken as the surface measure of the unit sphere, and
  4416	`sigma_s = s^2 map (w -> s w) sigma_1` as that of the radius-`s` sphere, so
  4417	`sigma_s/(4 pi s) = (s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) sigma_1`. Neither
  4418	identification with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure is proved.
  4419	The manuscript has `d in {1,2,3}` (`H:homog`) and `s >= 0`; the value zero for
  4420	other `d` and for `s <= 0` is a Lean convention (`waveGreen_other`,
  4421	`waveGreen_of_nonpos`), and every mass and scaling statement carries
  4422	`d = 1 \/ d = 2 \/ d = 3`, so no statement holds through it.

  1057	
  1058	Formalizes the rest of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
  1059	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `975feb3`: definitions
  1060	`E:damped-norm-definitions`, lines 745-755; lemma, lines 766-792, with the
  1061	tails `E:damped-tail-norms` at lines 785-788 and the smoothing sentence at
  1062	lines 789-791; proof, lines 793-846). The finiteness part and
  1063	`N_2(theta)^2 >= 0` were already formalized (`DampedNorms`, `ClockCopy`,
  1064	re-issued with nothing supplied in `ClockCopyHomog`). This module adds
  1065	`N_0(theta) = theta^(-2)`, the scaling identities
  1066	`N_1(theta) = theta^(alpha+alpha0-2) N_1(1)` and
  1067	`N_2(theta)^2 = theta^(-beta) N_2(1)^2` with `beta = 4-alpha-alpha0`, both
  1068	tails `N_1^(M)(1) -> 0` and `N_2^(M)(1) -> 0` of `E:damped-tail-norms`
  1069	(also `N_2^(M)(1)^2 -> 0` and the tail form `N_2^(M)(1)^2 >= 0`), and the
  1070	smoothing and truncation sentence. The wrapper
  1071	`damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` bundles all of these with the finiteness
  1072	part and `N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`. It assumes `H:homog`
  1073	(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, temporal
  1074	exponent `a = alpha0`) and NOT `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX, plus one
  1075	input, `GreenMass G`, used only by the `N_0` conclusions (discharged by
  1076	`WaveGreen`).
  1077	
  1078	Input of this module: `GreenMass G`, the mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` for `s > 0`
  1079	that the proof uses at line 825 (the TeX imports it from the source, Chen
  1080	(2.5)). This module defines no wave Green measure, so `N0 G theta` is
  1081	defined for an arbitrary family `G` of measures on `R^d` and `GreenMass G`
  1082	is exactly the identity the TeX uses, no stronger. All other conclusions of
  1083	the wrapper hold under `H:homog` alone (they do not use `GreenMass`). The
  1084	input is discharged in wave L6 by the module `WaveGreen` (section below):
  1085	`WaveGreen.waveGreen_greenMass` proves `GreenMass (waveGreen d)` for
  1086	`d = 1, 2, 3`, and `WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave` states the
  1087	lemma with nothing supplied.
  1088	
  1089	Reading of the smoothing sentence (Le's decision for wave L5, the default
  1090	answer adopted on 2026-11-11). "Spatial Gaussian smoothing" and "Gaussian
  1091	smoothing of the Green kernel" are read as a measurable multiplier
  1092	`g : R^d -> [0,1]` on the spectral measure: `mu` is replaced by
  1093	`g(xi) mu(dxi)` (`smoothed mu g`). Green smoothing `p_eta * G_s` multiplies
  1094	`G_s hat(xi) G_t hat(xi)` by `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)`, which depends on `xi`
  1095	only, so it is covered by this reading; the module does not define smoothed
  1096	Green kernels. "Restriction of a temporal Laplace domain" is read as
  1097	restricting the Laplace variable `lambda` to a measurable set `S` (all
  1098	`lambda`-integrals are over `S cap (0,inf)`): the first norm `N1on`, the
  1099	kernel `K_S` (`KS`) and the second norm `N2onSq`. The TeX uses the sentence
  1100	in this form at lines 1072-1082 (the Laplace domains `A_e`, Green
  1101	smoothing) and 1591-1600 (the Gaussian multipliers "can be removed in the
  1102	upper bounds"). The statement proved: for measurable `S subset S'` and
  1103	measurable `g <= 1`, the first and second norms of `g mu` restricted to `S`
  1104	are at most those of `mu` restricted to `S'`; `S' = (0,inf)` gives the full
  1105	norms (`N1on_univ`, `N2onSq_univ`), and `S' = (M,inf)`, `theta = 1` the
  1106	tail norms.
  1107	
  1108	Abstractions: `N1tail a M mu` and `K_M` (`KM`) integrate `lambda` over
  1109	`(M,inf) cap (0,inf)`, which is the TeX's `int_M^inf` for `M >= 0`; only
  1110	`M -> inf` is asserted. `N2tail` is `sqrt(N2tailSq)`, the printed form of
  1111	`E:damped-tail-norms`.
  1112	
  1113	Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values:
  1114	- Every integral the lemma asserts finite comes with an integrability
  1115	  conclusion (the `N_0` integrand, the tail integrands, the integrands of
  1116	  the smoothed and restricted norms), since a Lean Bochner integral of a
  1117	  non-integrable function is `0`. `N1_scaling` alone is an identity of Lean
  1118	  integrals; integrability is `DampedNorms.N1_integrable`.
  1119	- `K_S(0)` is a divergent integral for `S = (M,inf)`, and its Lean value is
  1120	  `0`. This happens only on the diagonal `s = t`, a `P2`-null set, so no
  1121	  statement depends on it; `integral_FKS_eq` holds at every `(s,t)` because
  1122	  both sides use the same totalized integral.
  1123	- `N2tail = sqrt(N2tailSq)` is not a junk square root under `H:homog`:
  1124	  `N2tailSq >= 0` is proved (`N2tail_props`). `N0` uses
  1125	  `(G s univ).toReal`, which equals `s` under `GreenMass` (no infinite-mass
  1126	  junk).
  1127	- The general lemmas state their side conditions: s-finiteness of `mu`,
  1128	  `mu`-integrability of `(1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1)`, `mu{0} = 0`, measurability of
  1129	  `g` and of `S`, `S'`, and `0 < a < 1`, `theta > 0`.
  1130	
  1131	Hypotheses of `H:homog` used by the wrapper: `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`,
  1132	`threshold`, `alpha_range` (for `alpha > 0`), `mu_radon`, and, through
  1133	`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, `mu_tempered`,
  1134	`spectral` and `scaling`. The fields `dim`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`,
  1135	`Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef` and `mu_even` are carried but unused.
  1136	
  1137	Proof route (differs from the TeX, same statements):
  1138	- `N_2` scaling: instead of changing `(s,t,xi)` in the spectral formula, both
  1139	  sides are written as `int_0^inf w_theta` (`ClockCopy.K_eq_integral_weight`)
  1140	  and the one-dimensional substitution `lambda = theta u` is combined with
  1141	  `w_theta(theta u) = theta^(a+alpha-5) w_1(u)` (`weight_scaling`). `N_1`
  1142	  scaling uses the same substitution and `R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1)`.
  1143	- Tails and truncation: instead of dominated convergence in `(s,t,xi)`, the
  1144	  subordinated integrand `DampedNorms.FK` is restricted to `lambda in S`
  1145	  (`FKS`) and Fubini gives `N_S(theta)^2 = int_(S cap (0,inf)) w_theta`
  1146	  (`N2onSq_eq`). The tail limit is the tail of the integrable `w_1`, and
  1147	  nonnegativity is `w_theta >= 0` (the TeX uses positive definiteness of the
  1148	  tail kernel). The facts `0 <= K_M <= |r|^(-alpha0)` and `K_M(r) -> 0` for
  1149	  `r != 0` used by the TeX are proved (`KS_nonneg`, `KS_le`, `KM_tendsto`)
  1150	  but are not needed by this route.
  1151	- Smoothing: instead of removing the multiplier from the nonnegative
  1152	  quadratic form at each `xi`, the weights are compared at each `lambda`
  1153	  (`weight_smoothed_le`), since `w_theta(lambda)` is a `mu`-integral of a
  1154	  nonnegative function of `xi`; for `N_1`, `R_(g mu) <= R_mu`
  1155	  (`resolvent_smoothed_le`).
  1156	
  1157	Narrower conclusions: smoothing is covered only in the multiplier reading
  1158	above (no smoothed Green kernel or smoothed covariance is built); `N_0` is
  1159	proved here for any family `G` satisfying `GreenMass G`; for the wave Green
  1160	measures it is `WaveGreen.N0_waveGreen`, with nothing supplied. The tails
  1161	are stated at `theta = 1`, as in the TeX; the restricted norms are stated
  1162	for every `theta > 0`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to
  1163	the Lean proof route)"; the definition `FKS` only names the restricted

    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)
   104

   173	\section{Model and standing assumptions}\label{S:model}
   174	
   175	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   176	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   177	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   178	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   179	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   180	\end{equation}
   181	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   182	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   183	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   184	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   185	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   186	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   187	\end{equation}
   188	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   189	
   190	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   191	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   192	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   193	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   194	  convention
   195	  \[
   196	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   197	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   198	  \]
   199	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   200	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}
   205	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   206	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   207	\end{hypothesis}
   208	
   209	\paragraph{Zero covariance.}
   210	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} allows $\Gamma = 0$ by design. In this case the
   211	centered Gaussian noise is $\W = 0$, and the solution with initial data
   212	$(1,0)$ is $u(t,x) = 1$. Thus $\E|u(t,x)|^p = 1$ for every $p > 0$, and
   213	all normalized logarithmic moment rates are zero. Results asserting strict
   214	positivity of covariance-dependent quantities impose $\Gamma \ne 0$ locally.
   215	
   216	Throughout we write
   217	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   218	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   219	\end{equation}
   220	
   221	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   222	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   223	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   224	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   225	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   226	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   227	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   228	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   229	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   230	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   231	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   232	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
   233	the full moment supremum. The earlier results discussed below concern different
   330	auxiliary sections. In particular, our uses of the latter cite Theorem~1.1, not
   331	Corollary~1.2. Thus, neither a disputed first-moment constant nor an auxiliary
   332	static coefficient theorem enters the interval-field upper bound.

    61	    μ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ alpha) * μ A
